# KS-1131 — Wednesday's task for Ornith (written 2026-09-25 10:10 from the file at origin develop `6ab9d5021e96ea1481cb6c6ff2d6d33b414aecb7` — the file read WHOLE, 327 lines) — item 2 (F-B) ONLY, CODE_PATCH, **ONE file, MODIFIED IN PLACE, two hunks, SELF-TESTING**

File: `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts`
Tip: `6ab9d5021e96ea1481cb6c6ff2d6d33b414aecb7`
Runner: `vitest`

Written against the tip AS IT IS: **item 1 (F-A) has NOT merged** (its READY is held, `READY_KS-1131-…PASS-7of7_2026-09-25.diff.md`), so this brief carries NONE of F-A's lines and every number below is the tip's. The file at this tip is byte-identical to the file at `2bc5ccf63` that the F-A brief was written from (`cmp` = 0), last changed at `fa55e58c9` (2026-09-13, PR #970). Both hunks here are region-disjoint from F-A's two hunks (`:216-:220`, `:262-:265`) and from each other; F-A's `NL` / `resetHandler` names are NOT reused, so the two briefs stack in either order (measured, see Premises).

## THE MODE — read this twice

**CODE_PATCH, ONE file, MODIFIED IN PLACE** (`--- a/<path>` / `+++ b/<path>`, the path exactly as on the `File:` line above). There is no new file and no second file. This file is BOTH the product (its helper `assertConsumeIsGuarded` at `:193-:220` is the structural check KS-1131 is about) and the suite that grades it, so the fix and the cells that pin it land in the same file, in two region-disjoint hunks.

## Self-testing — test hunks: 2

The checker applies **hunk 2 (E2, the new cells) ALONE at the tip — the declared red cell must go RED** — then **hunk 1 (E1, the fix) on top — it must go GREEN**. Keep the two hunks in this order: E1 first (`@@ -203`), E2 second (`@@ -223`).

## What is wrong (one paragraph)

`assertConsumeIsGuarded` (`:193-:220`) is the check behind the two KS-963 cells at `:223` and `:228`. Its PROPERTY 1 exists to prove the single-use-token consume sits INSIDE the `if (!user) {` block. Its assertion, **`:206`** — `  expect(guardBody).toContain(consumeFn);` — looks for the raw NAME in the raw brace-matched block, so a block whose consume was DELETED and replaced by a comment that merely MENTIONS `consumeResetToken` still passes, and property 2 cannot catch it (the count before the lookup is still 1). The gate's F-B, measured (R13): `// consumeResetToken deliberately not called here any more` in place of the call leaves 13/13 GREEN. This task adds, directly above `:206`, an assertion that the guard block contains a CALL-SHAPED occurrence (`consumeFn + '('`) — the ticket's own offered fix shape ("or count call-shaped matches"), the same shape as item 1 — and adds two cells that feed the helper a synthetic handler: one whose `!user` block holds only that comment (RED at the tip, GREEN after), one whose `!user` block holds a real consume (green on both trees). **NOT in this task:** item 1 (F-A, `:219`), item 3 (F-C, `:256`), item 4 (P2, the wallet slice); `:206` itself is untouched and stays (it is implied by the new line; see UNMEASURED 2).

## The exact change — 2 SMALL EDITS (≤ 3), each its own hunk

**E1 (hunk 1, header `@@ -203,4 +203,5 @@`)** — a PURE INSERTION of ONE `+` line between `:205` (`  expect(guardBody).not.toBe('');`) and `:206` (`  expect(guardBody).toContain(consumeFn);`). Leading context `:203-:205`, trailing context `:206` (2 spaces each). `:207` is blank, which is why `:206` is NOT edited in place: the new line goes ABOVE it.

```
@@ -203,4 +203,5 @@
   // somewhere after it. A sibling occurrence cannot satisfy this.
   const guardBody = braceBlock(src, guard);
   expect(guardBody).not.toBe('');
+  expect(guardBody).toContain(consumeFn + '(');
   expect(guardBody).toContain(consumeFn);
```

**E2 (hunk 2, header `@@ -223,3 +224,29 @@`)** — a PURE INSERTION of 26 `+` lines placed BEFORE `:223` (the `it(` line of the reset-token cell, the first cell of the `KS-963 widened` describe that opens at `:222`). The `+` lines come FIRST and the context `:223-:225` AFTER them. The new lines sit INSIDE that describe, so `assertConsumeIsGuarded` (file scope, `:193`) is in scope. **No blank `+` line anywhere.**

```
@@ -223,3 +224,29 @@
+  // KS-1131 F-B: a comment naming the consume inside the !user block is not a consume.
+  const LF = String.fromCharCode(10);
+  const guardedHandler = (guardLine: string) =>
+    [
+      'router.post(PATH, async (req, res) => {',
+      '  const stored = await userRepo.getResetToken(tokenHash);',
+      '  if (new Date() > stored.expiresAt) {',
+      '    await userRepo.consumeResetToken(tokenHash);',
+      '    return res.status(400).json({ error: 1 });',
+      '  }',
+      '  const user = await userRepo.getUserByIdPreAuth(stored.userId);',
+      '  if (!user) {',
+      guardLine,
+      '    return res.status(404).json({ error: 2 });',
+      '  }',
+      '  await userRepo.consumeResetToken(tokenHash);',
+      '});',
+    ].join(LF);
+  it('KS-1131 F-B a comment naming the consume inside the !user block is NOT a guarded consume', () => {
+    const src = guardedHandler('    // consumeResetToken deliberately not called here any more');
+    expect(() => assertConsumeIsGuarded(src, 'consumeResetToken', 0)).toThrow();
+  });
+  it('KS-1131 F-B CONTROL a real consume inside the !user block still satisfies the helper', () => {
+    const src = guardedHandler('    await userRepo.consumeResetToken(tokenHash);');
+    expect(() => assertConsumeIsGuarded(src, 'consumeResetToken', 0)).not.toThrow();
+  });
   it('the reset-token consume is INSIDE the !user branch, so a throw precedes it', async () => {
     const src = await readRoute('auth.ts');
     assertConsumeIsGuarded(src, 'consumeResetToken', 0);
```

**Every `+` line is ASCII only and carries NO backslash, NO backtick, NO double-quote character and NO `$`** (counted by the writer over all 27 `+` lines: 0 of each; 0 blank). The newline between the synthetic lines is `String.fromCharCode(10)` precisely so that no `+` line needs a backslash. The comment string in the RED cell deliberately has NO `(` after `consumeResetToken`. The names are `LF` and `guardedHandler` ON PURPOSE: item 1 uses `NL` and `resetHandler` in the same describe, and a repeated `const` would not compile once both land. Do not "improve" any of it.

**Do NOT change:** `:206` (stays, as E1's trailing context), `:193-:205` and `:207-:220` (the helper's other lines, including `:219`, which is item 1's), the three existing cells `:223-:264`, the `KS-963 r2` describe `:287-:327`, `braceBlock` (`:146-:182`), `count` (`:184`), `readRoute` (`:186-:187`), the imports and the header comment. Do NOT rename the new cells: the checker names the red one by its literal title.

## Where (parsed into the checklist — every **must change** line must appear as a `-` line in your diff)

* `:206` — (correct) `  expect(guardBody).toContain(consumeFn);` — stays; E1 is INSERT-ONLY and is anchored ABOVE it, so it has no must-change line
* `:205` — (correct) `  expect(guardBody).not.toBe('');` — stays (context)
* `:223` — (correct) `  it('the reset-token consume is INSIDE the !user branch, so a throw precedes it', async () => {` — stays; E2 is INSERT-ONLY and is anchored ABOVE it

## THIS IS VITEST

`services/auth/package.json` `"test": "vitest"`. The file already imports what it needs from `'vitest'`; **add no import**, `vi.mock` nothing new, never write `jest.*`.

## The test — TWO new cells in the EXISTING suite (no new file)

File: `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts`
The input's `reference_test` is `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/s130-f6-openapi-module-in-the-import-graph.test.ts` — a small sibling in the same folder that needs no mock and no database. **You do not edit it.** The shape to copy is this file's own: the new cells call the file-scope helper `assertConsumeIsGuarded(src, consumeFn, lookupFrom)` (`:193`) on a SOURCE STRING, exactly as the cells at `:225` and `:237` call it on `auth.ts`'s text — no I/O, no mock, no app boot.

Cells (every cell RED or CONTROL, nothing optional):
- RED `it('KS-1131 F-B a comment naming the consume inside the !user block is NOT a guarded consume')`: a synthetic reset handler whose `if (!user) {` block holds only a `//` comment naming `consumeResetToken` must make the helper throw. **At the untouched tip this cell FAILS**: `:206` finds the name in the comment, property 2 counts 1 before the lookup, the helper does not throw, and `toThrow()` fails by assertion. It passes only with E1, which finds no `consumeResetToken(` in the block. That is the red.
- CONTROL `it('KS-1131 F-B CONTROL a real consume inside the !user block still satisfies the helper')`: the same handler with a real `await userRepo.consumeResetToken(tokenHash);` in the `!user` block must NOT make the helper throw — green on both trees.
- CONTROL (existing, untouched) `:223` and `:228`: the real `auth.ts` still satisfies the helper on both trees.

## Red cells

- KS-1131 F-B a comment naming the consume inside the !user block is NOT a guarded consume

## Output

Exactly ONE ```diff block, nothing outside it: `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts` / `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts`, then the TWO hunks above exactly as shown (`@@ -203,4 +203,5 @@`, then `@@ -223,3 +224,29 @@`), in that order. Every `+` line is its OWN physical line (the INPUT JSON shows this brief's line breaks as the two characters backslash and n inside a JSON string — DECODE them; a `+` line that carries a backslash is a FAIL). Every context line keeps its leading space.

## Premises (measured at the tip named above, 2026-09-25 10:0x)

- **The anchors.** `:203-:206` and `:223-:225` byte for byte as quoted (read with `git show 6ab9d5021e96:… | cat -n`); non-ASCII count 0 on each of those lines (`:222`, the describe line, carries an em dash, which is why E2 has no leading context). `:206` is byte-unique (`grep -cF` = 1); the `:223` line is byte-unique (1). `:207` is blank (why E1 anchors above `:206`).
- **Hunk shape.** Counted: E1 old 4 / new 5, E2 old 3 / new 29; `+` lines 27, of which double-quote 0, backslash 0, backtick 0, `$` 0, non-ASCII 0, blank 0. `selftest_split.py FB.diff 2` → `TEST [2] (30 lines) · PROD [1] (6 lines)`.
- **Applies.** `patch --dry-run -F0 -p1` of the whole diff at the tip: rc 0. `git apply --check -p1` (strict, the checker's A2) of the whole diff: rc 0. The checker's A4 leg (the TEST half ALONE via `git apply`): rc 0 (`Hunk #1 succeeded at 223`); the A5 leg (PROD on top): rc 0; the result is byte-identical to the whole diff applied with `patch`.
- **Stacks with item 1.** F-A's fence then this one, and this one then F-A's, both apply with `patch -F0` (rc 0 each) and give byte-identical 381-line files; F-A applied then this brief's TEST half alone: rc 0.
- **The red and the controls were EXECUTED, not reasoned.** Wednesday's drafter lifted, programmatically and VERBATIM from each patched copy of this file, everything from `function braceBlock` through the close of the `KS-963 widened` describe (so `braceBlock`, `count`, `readRoute`, `assertConsumeIsGuarded` and every cell in that describe, as patched), ran it in node 24 (type stripping) with a minimal `describe`/`it`/`expect` shim, against the real `routes/auth.ts` and `routes/wallet.ts` at this tip. Results: TEST half alone at the tip → the F-B red cell FAILS (`AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw an error`), the F-B control and all three existing cells PASS; TEST + PROD → all 5 PASS; with F-A merged first, TEST half alone → the F-B red FAILS, the other 6 PASS; F-A + F-B → all 7 PASS. (A simulation with a shim, not a vitest run — the checker's run is the measurement.)
- **The fix catches R13 on the REAL file.** With `auth.ts:838` (the `!user` consume in the reset handler) replaced by the R13 comment: the unfixed helper → the `:223` cell PASSES (the defect, reproduced); the fixed helper → it FAILS with `expected <string> to contain "consumeResetToken("`.
- **Why `consumeFn + '('` is safe on the real file.** `auth.ts` at this tip: `consumeResetToken(` and `consumeEmailToken(` each occur 3 times, and each occurs 3 times raw, so all are calls; both `!user` blocks (`:837-:838`, `:883-:884`) hold a real call.
- **Surface.** A structural unit suite that reads `routes/*.ts` as text. No network, no database, no credential. **Not an auth PRODUCT edit**: `auth.ts` is read, never edited.

## UNMEASURED — stated rather than glossed

1. **No vitest run and no `build_input.sh` run.** The builder's fence gates (blank context, leading-only insertion, context-as-addition, undeclared red) were checked by reading their source against this fence, not by running the builder; prettier was not run (the raise seat formats).
2. **`:206` is kept, so the block now asserts both the raw and the call-shaped name.** The raw one is implied by the new one; deleting it needs the blank `:207` as context, which the builder refuses. A later tidy may drop it.
3. **Call-shaped matching has a residual in both directions:** a comment in the `!user` block that writes the name WITH a paren (`// consumeResetToken(x) was here`) still satisfies property 1 (a false green that survives), and a real call written with a space before the paren would red (a false red, the safe direction; prettier never emits it). The comment-and-string stripper the ticket also offers is the stronger fix and is NOT this task.
4. **`patch(1)` on the TEST half alone fails** (`1 out of 1 hunks failed`, Apple patch 2.0, `-F0`, `-F3` and the default alike): E2 has no leading context and `patch` anchors such a lone hunk at the start of the file. The checker applies halves with `git apply`, which accepts it (measured above), and the whole diff applies with `patch -F0`. Only a hand-split with `patch` would trip on it.

## Collision

`ks963-preauth-rethrow.test.ts` is named by exactly one held READY: KS-1131 item 1 (F-A), region-disjoint from both hunks here, stacking measured clean in both orders. KS-1131 has 3 rows in `night/done.md`, all item 1 (two A3c FAILs from the harness emoji fault, one PASS 7/7). Items 3 (F-C) and 4 (P2) change `:243`/`:256`-`:259`, disjoint from both hunks here.
